## Identify the target from real pool acceptance

Do not gate the literal second `/v3/admissions` call. With the all-f prospect target, prospect-only proofs can precede either block win and must retain their normal behavior. Observe fully validated original `/pool/v3/submit` or `/pool/v3/lookup` success envelopes in the relay, tied to the selected source/money/profile and exact original job/nonce/header/work hash. The target is the fighter admission for the **second accepted pool-winning receipt**, with accepted sequence2, after the first pool winner's fighter admission has completed normally.

`pool_delivery.go` broadcasts and verifies a block before pool delivery and fighter signing, and synchronizes the original authorization before the admission call. However, `deliverPool` can return nil while retaining a pending pool result and then proceed to fighter delivery. Therefore an admission call alone does not prove accepted pool work. A candidate target without its already observed second accepted receipt fails this finite attempt; the harness must not wait for the blocked worker to create that receipt, manually submit it, fabricate a busy response, or substitute another proof.

The relay holds the exact target request **before forwarding upstream**. It forwards all unrelated admission traffic unchanged. During this short hold, read the original operator's public status: both original public/round readiness prerequisites must be present, source intake must be `draining` with the exact `pool_capacity` reason and submissions2, and no hard admission/publication hold may be present. Keep dated status observations. The two captured original canonical receipts and the later closed source census must agree. Failure to observe these facts inside the hold is a failure, not permission to extend the request.

Prior A3 evidence supplies no completed second drain-delivery proof: its second retained row was unsigned/pool pending at stop. This plan deliberately lets that target finish block publication, pool acceptance and synchronized fighter authorization first. It makes no assumption that the complete outbox has only two rows or that all other fighters are settled.

## Case A: admission after drain, lost reply, original historical replay

1. After the full-intake/readiness observation, release the one exact held admission to the original server while its original job is live. Require its genuine successful response to contain `Inserted=true`, the original proof/authorization, original issuance-time birth and the canonical-winning-block eligibility. Record the original authenticated response before deliberately losing that one reply; never manufacture a response.
2. Stop and join the original CLI promptly. If the same target retries before Stop completes, hold only that exact replay before forwarding, under the same per-call bound, and cancel/join it. A retry that already completed would not prove a retained lost acknowledgment and fails this scenario. Unrelated requests remain independently recorded.
3. Stop/join the original operator and all relevant relay handlers before opening any audit owner. Full selected original issuer/source/outbox audits must show the exact target signature still pending locally and exactly one corresponding admitted record/receipt/ownership outbox item at the authority. The original publisher may already have progressed that item, so use the complete original publication census rather than assuming its live queue still contains an unprocessed row.
4. Reopen the same physical operator and attachment roots, retain the complete target identity, and reestablish original readiness with mining still drained. Restart the production CLI and permit the exact retained target replay. Require the original historical record/birth/receipt to match the lost success, with `Inserted=false` and historical eligibility semantics. Then stop/join and audit the durable local accepted result. No second target admission, authorization or birth is allowed. This actual case need not wait for expiry; the separate component controls prove historical-first behavior after expiry and hard hold.

The actual proof establishes the original record/census and immutable response. The frozen component tests separately establish the zero new clock/node calls of the historical branch; do not claim unobserved internal calls from relay silence.

## Case B: never forwarded, stopped through real expiry

1. Reach the same target, second accepted pool receipt and original full-intake/readiness observation. Keep the target admission unforwarded. Stop the original CLI within its original request deadline, join its pipes and the canceled relay handler, and record that this target was never sent upstream.
2. Stop/join the operator. Full closed original audits must prove the exact signed target remains pending locally, both canonical pool receipts remain accepted, and no matching fighter record, receipt, ownership-admission entry or publication exists. Preserve all unrelated prior admissions; the zero claim is for this exact target, not the entire issuer.
3. Wait the remaining actual original job lifetime with the worker stopped. No HTTP request remains held during this wait. Record actual wall time at or beyond the captured expiry, without clock substitution.
4. Reopen the same original operator/attachment and restart the production CLI. The original authenticated submission of that exact signed proof must return definite `expired` with `outcome_unknown=false`, through the original issuer clock/persistence/session path. Require a durable expired local target after Stop/join and another stopped reopen, unchanged authorization/job/proof, and still zero matching birth/receipt/publication. Capacity, busy, unknown or any mixed failure is not a terminal substitute.

## Retained identity, finite requests and financial scope

The unchanged worker reconciles retained entries before considering new work. After that call returns, an empty scan can lead it to create unrelated recoverable request rows; a durable `not_issued` result currently continues the loop rather than setting the in-memory capacity pause. Consequently, do **not** infer globally unchanged q counts from a completed admission call or race Stop to assert that. Preserve the target's original request/job/signature, report every additional terminal or pending q row under the existing MaxRequests/shared outbox bounds, and require that draining creates no additional issued job/work. No new request is used to replace, resign or reclassify the target. Root explicitly selected this per-target interpretation before any actual freeze or execution; no worker change is proposed. Continued post-drain terminal-request consumption remains finite-capacity debt: it can exhaust the remaining request/shared outbox budget, which this proof neither replenishes nor solves.

Both source rewards must be actually accepted for this drain proof; the one-reward branch is not a passing substitute. Subject to the unchanged independent two-reward fixture assumptions, reuse its exact total payout1,980,000,000 atoms, fee209 and change19,999,791, one original batch and the original recipient. Record actual funding values and reject a changed reward/fee premise rather than using Go output as expected arithmetic. No second-day payment, partial payout subset or cap enlargement is permitted.

After the retained admission phase, the stopped original wallet may observe the original real-UTC scheduled payout through the inherited actual helper. For Case B this demonstrates that fighter expiry does not revoke either accepted pool reward. Original pending batch body/raw/txid/claims remain byte-identical across any recovery, with only allowed delivery state progress. Fighter admission itself invokes no settlement dispatch; component tests prove its zero quote/sign/send effect. Count original scheduler broadcasts separately and require one exact complete payout. A whole-frontier D84 refusal is preserved by the component suite, not simulated by this two-input actual.

## Public evidence and cleanup

Freeze source/selection/lock/checker identities before each attempt. Record bounded public target request/response canonical hashes, original job/proof/authorization and expiry, the two pool receipts, the exact status samples, hold/forward/drop/replay times and outcomes, every CLI/operator generation and join, and complete closed source/issuer/outbox/financial projections. Use existing full read-only owners, close them, then bounded `StrictAll` public projections with before/after identities. Never inspect live DBs or expose credentials, raw headers, private wallet data or tokens.

The relay only delays or loses a selected genuine exchange; it supplies no admission, node, signing or clock authority. No account/outbox lock is retained by the harness across network work. Keep original one-Wait/sticky-cleanup process ownership and original TERM/KILL group cleanup. All handler/process joins and failed-close owners must be reported. Any missing evidence, extra target insertion, unknown result, failed cleanup, expired live acceptance, altered signature or source drift fails the attempt and is preserved.

This is a finite candidate test of original-job fighter delivery at pool-only drain. It does not prove continuous capacity, authority rollover, arbitrary hard-cap admission, production custody, host deployment or broad public readiness. Hard-hold escalation, prospect-only eligibility and failure-provenance precedence remain separately covered by the frozen component acceptance table.
